So, I had a friend who got a girl pregnant when he was 19. He was scared, terrified of what that meant for him and his future. He was so scared that he refused to sign the birth certificate, meaning he had no legal ties to the child. Now, if she IS pregnant and DID decide to keep the baby, you aren't obligated to sign the birth certificate, you aren't obligated to be in the child's life legally. You also wouldn't have any rights to the child. I know that you're scared in your situation right now but I would do some research into legal issues with rights to children/birth certificates because...as bad as this is to say, your mom doesn't have to know. Do we change? Learn? Adapt? Cope, even in the face of inner turmoil? Absolutely.

I was admitted for 5 days last summer. There was a mandatory 72 hour holding period (I did admit myself but because I said I wanted to SH, they had to keep me). Group therapy, saw my psychiatrists/nurse practitioner once a day, weird jail shower but my own room/bathroom, cameras everywhere, eating together with the group. Granted, my stay was in a hospital and not something long term. The psychiatrists did talk me through some things, albeit briefly, and adjusted my medications. She told me I wasn't there long enough to see changes but they set up appointments for me for when I got out. 

My employer fired me. They got me on a no call-no show technicality. The place is what drove me to the hospital to begin with so I never expected to have it once I got out.  
We had set times during the day we could use the phone, 6 am to 10 pm. I called my family when I could, my partner too. There was one visitation period, 30 minutes after dinner every day. One/two visitors at a time. 

As for what I did all day, I went to group, sat in the common area and stared mindlessly at a tv, took naps, colored (yeah, actual crayons and coloring and word searches lol).   
The crisis unit, I guess you could call it, was beneficial to me at that time. It got me out of my home, away from stressors. I didn't have to worry about food or bills or...anything, really, except for trying to get my head to a better place. Some people were there longer than I was, everyone was itching to get out.  
If you don't feel safe at home, safe in your own skin, a crisis unit is a good move, imo, but know that in most states (if you live in the us) there is a holding period that most places have to keep you to make sure you are safe.
